subject: Probe signals and governance runway for Clearbyte eval

Cc: Clara Zhou <clara.zhou@clearbyte.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Probe signals and governance runway for Clearbyte eval

Evan / Clara —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation, I sketched a minimal, evidence-driven plan that defines how we’ll judge success during the 6-week evaluation and what we’ll need from ClearByte to make a decision at the end of the runway. The attached PDF is the short-form plan (two pages) and there’s a live sheet with smoke test scripts in the Drive link below.

High-level asks:
- Week 0: baseline dataset, one sandbox tenant with ~10k users anonymized, and a primary SRE contact for limited testing windows.
- Weeks 1–4: targeted workloads (search ranking + conversational support) with three predetermined traffic profiles (low/med/peak).
- Week 5: smoke verification (automated scripts + handbook walkthrough).
- Week 6: decision review call — passbands defined below.

Proposed passbands (quick):
- Precision @Top3 > 78% on labeled sample A OR F1 > 0.70 on support classification task.
- 95th percentile tail latency < 450ms for interactive flows at medium profile.
- Service continuity: no more than 1 recoverable incident attributable to model serving in evaluation window.

If ClearByte agrees, we’ll run the verification scripts the week before the review and I’ll bring Ben (solutions) and Marissa (AM) to the decision call.

Attachments: clearbyte-eval-probe-signals-v1.pdf (2 pages), smoke-test-scripts.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/clearbyte-eval
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/CB-2026-1127

Cheers,

From: Evan Myers <evan.myers@clearbyte.com>

Cc: Clara Zhou <clara.zhou@clearbyte.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Probe signals and governance runway for Clearbyte eval

Vanessa —

Appreciate the crisp plan and the PDF. Quick questions from our side before we lock the schedule:
1) The 10k anonymized users — can we provide a smaller superset (3k) for week 1 and scale up to 10k by week 3? We have masking automation but need to validate at smaller scale first.
2) For the latency target: is the 450ms 95th percentile based on cold-starts included, or only for warmed endpoints?
3) On the incident allowance: would a single brief degradation during a load test count, or are you specifically calling out production-affecting incidents?

We’re generally aligned on the metrics. I’ll loop procurement once we confirm the timeline so they can prep the temporary access SLA.

— Evan
Evan Myers
Head of ML Ops
ClearByte
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Evan Myers <evan.myers@clearbyte.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Clara Zhou <clara.zhou@clearbyte.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 13:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Probe signals and governance runway for Clearbyte eval

Evan — good questions; short answers inline below.

1) Scale ramp — yes, that’s fine. Week 1 can start at ~3k; we’ll set the test harness to scale traffic and KV cache warm-up so week 3 reflects the 10k profile. We’ll note the step-up in the verification log so it’s auditable.
2) Latency target — the 95th percentile excludes cold-starts. We’ll define warm-window criteria (endpoint has processed > 30 requests in the last 10 minutes). We can include a separate cold-start metric if you want.
3) Incident allowance — production-affecting incidents only. Brief recoverable degradations during controlled load tests are considered tolerated as long as they’re annotated and reproduced in the incident log.

Next steps:
- Ben, can you prepare the smoke-test script runbook and estimate how long the verification window will take?
- Marissa, please prepare a short mutual-action summary we can share with ClearByte procurement when they join.

I’ll update the attached PDF with the ramp note and the warm-window definition and resend.

Thanks —
Vanessa

Subject: Re: Probe signals and governance runway for Clearbyte eval

Vanessa / team —

I’ve attached a short runbook excerpt to this thread (I’ll drop the full runbook in the shared Drive). Quick notes:
- Estimated verification time for smoke scripts at medium profile: 90–120 minutes, including log capture and KV cache pre-warm.
- We’ll mark the warm-window as >=30 requests in 10 minutes (matches Vanessa).
- For reproducibility, collect three artifact types during each smoke run: (1) request/response traces (sampled at 1%), (2) model output snapshots for the labeled sample set, and (3) system metrics (GPU utilization, mem, tail latencies).

I suggest we set the formal decision criteria doc as: PASS / CONDITIONAL-PASS / FAIL, with conditional-pass including a short remediation backlog and a one-week follow-up verification. I’ll work with Priyom to produce the conditional-pass template.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
